subject: general
question: A man rows downstream to some destination and returns in 3 hours. If the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the stream are 6 km/h and 3 km/h, respectively, then the distance of the destination from the starting place is:
solution:
**Given:**

Boat speed = 6 km/h;

Stream speed = 3 km/h;

Total time = 3 hours

**Concept used:**

Time = Distance/Speed;

Distance downstream = (Boat speed + Stream speed) × Time;

Distance upstream = (Boat speed - Stream speed) × Time

**Calculation:**

Determine the downstream and upstream speeds.

Downstream speed = 6 km/h + 3 km/h = 9 km/h

Upstream speed = 6 km/h - 3 km/h = 3 km/h

Let the distance of Downstream and Upstream be 'x' km.

According to the formula,

x/9 + x/3 = 3

⇒ (x + 3x) / 9 = 3 

⇒ 4x = 27 

⇒ x = 6.75 km.

**∴ The distance of the destination from the starting place is 6.75 km.**
